note: Milestone 70, 70A: the delivery owner's review of tests/baseline/ms70-declaration-dispositions.json. The draft places each declaration by the monolith section it sits in; the review found that rule wrong for 94 declarations (sections whose banner no longer describes what is under them) and one disposition (_visitedPages, dead). scripts/ms70-declaration-dispositions.mjs applies these overrides and marks a declaration reviewed only while its disposition and delivery still match what is recorded here, so a declaration that appears later starts unreviewed and fails tests/unit/ms70-declaration-dispositions.spec.js.
method: Every section's declarations were read against the plan's delivery scopes (MILESTONE-70-PROPOSAL.md, 'Delivery map'); every delete-as-dead and test-only candidate was searched for by name across src, index.html, fragments, help and tests, markup and window reads included; each duplicate keeps its duplicateOf module as the canonical home.

why.state-owner: The case-state root. 70E adopts a store seam while this stays the owner; the declaration goes when the module store becomes the sole owner (70J), not with the section it happens to sit in.
why.router-state: Navigation state the router owns (src/core/navigation/router.js reads and writes it); moves with the router in 70K.
why.persistence: Save, auto-save, export-dirty tracking, template loading or the continue prompt -- persistence and startup (70I), not the section it sits in.
why.store-seam: An accessor modules call to read case state: exactly what 70E's store seam replaces.
why.shell: Sidebar, header, picker or tab-coordination UI -- a shell controller (70H). The router banner above it is historical: the router itself moved to src/core/navigation/router.js.
why.registry: Filing-type registry data, a blank factory or a normalizer: 70C's scope (normalizeWardData is the .sav-load normalizer).
why.pure: A pure calculation or formatter with no DOM or state: 70B.
why.form-runtime: Form-field markup, field helpers or collection add/remove actions -- the shared form runtime (70F). They sit in the feature-bridge sections only because they were left behind when each feature was extracted.
why.bridge: A feature bridge like the other seven, which move together in 70K; the Simplified one sits in the Guardian wizard's section by accident.
why.dead-visited: Dead on both sides: a `let` is never a window property, so the three module references (router.js add, ward-lifecycle.js clear x2) read window._visitedPages as undefined and never run, and the monolith never reads it. Delete it and those three references together in 70E.
why.writes-classic-state: Assigns the monolith's own `let activeInventoryType` (and updates the sidebar and saves), which no module can do while that binding lives in the classic script; it moves when the binding does (70J). Its pure half is already src/core/filing/filing-descriptor.js's applyAccountingFilingType().
why.completion-data: The Initial Inventory's eleven schedule route keys, which the completion evaluators read; a model constant, it moved to src/core/filing/models/guardian.js with them.
why.nav-dom: Applies the completion map to the page -- the sidebar marks, section collapse, the Next button -- which the plan gives 70F's form runtime ('nav-dot updates, section collapse'), with applyNavSectionCollapse() and renderProgressSummary() that it calls. 70D moved the rules these read; they reach them through the monolith's computeNavChecks() dispatcher until then.
why.dispatcher: A one-line dispatcher that nothing in the monolith calls any more, kept because the dashboard still captures it off window (with getWardHeadlineTotal(), 70K). The evaluator it forwards to needs the Initial Inventory's validator, which exists only once that feature has loaded, and errorRoute() (70F): the monolith hands both in until 70K's feature context can. The plan allows the old function as a delegating dispatcher meanwhile; it goes when the dashboard's read does.
why.filing-workflow: The Add Form, Simplified Accounting eligibility and Delete Form dialogs and their handlers: creating a filing (what it carries over, the case it joins), the eligibility questions that choose Simplified or Annual, and deleting one -- the workflow 70G moves (the plan names eligibility, and its gate needs creation and deletion to go through the filing lifecycle service), not the modal plumbing their section is named for. That (showModal(), closeModal(), ensureFragment(), the ward-name combobox) stays for 70H.
why.store-forwarder: A one-line forwarder onto the case store or a module's totals, through src/legacy-bridge.js: since 70J the module store owns the case, so the monolith's remaining readers of the open filing, its type or a filing's Inventory totals reach them this way. It goes with those readers.
